Playbook.name: ACH — Maker-Checker Self-Approval (Segregation-of-Duties Violation) - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: In the ACH payment app, the same user was both maker and checker of a transaction (USERNAME_MAKER == USERNAME_CHECKER) - a segregation-of-duties violation enabling unauthorised/fraudulent payments. Triage: fraud/SoD breach, or a maker-checker config gap?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Maker-checker self-approval lets one person create AND approve payments - the core control failure behind payment fraud.

LogSources.LogSource: ACH/ECC application audit via apps-* - apps-*

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Banking-app audit in apps-* (verified live). ACH maker-checker fields USERNAME_MAKER/USERNAME_CHECKER; ECC user-admin type ECC_USR_AUDIT. type field distinguishes app streams (ACHAPP, ECC_USR_AUDIT).

Input.name: $user
Input.description: The user acting as both maker and checker (USERNAME_MAKER).

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance, not any single fact.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the self-approval is a fraud/SoD breach or a configuration/emergency-process gap.

Step.name: Self-approved ACH transactions by this user
Step.Purpose: The transactions where one user is both maker and checker, and their value, define the SoD breach.
Step.Query: FROM apps-* | WHERE type == "ACHAPP" AND USERNAME_MAKER == "$user" AND USERNAME_MAKER == USERNAME_CHECKER AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, USERNAME_MAKER, USERNAME_CHECKER, type | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: Each row where MAKER == CHECKER is a self-approval. Multiple, or high-value, self-approvals indicate deliberate fraud; a single one may be an emergency-process or config gap. Correlate with the transaction value/beneficiary in the app.

Step.name: This user's broader ACH maker/checker activity
Step.Purpose: A pattern of self-approvals vs a one-off separates deliberate fraud from an exception.
Step.Query: FROM apps-* | WHERE type == "ACHAPP" AND (USERNAME_MAKER == "$user" OR USERNAME_CHECKER == "$user") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS total = COUNT(*), self_approvals = COUNT(CASE(USERNAME_MAKER == USERNAME_CHECKER, 1, null)) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: A repeated self-approval pattern is deliberate SoD circumvention (fraud risk); a single instance may be an exception - still a control breach.

Node.Condition: Repeated or high-value maker==checker self-approvals - deliberate SoD circumvention.
Node.Result: True Positive (Payment Fraud / SoD Breach - escalate to fraud/compliance)

Node.Condition: A one-off self-approval due to a documented emergency process, low value, benign.
A maker-checker configuration gap allowing self-approval (control weakness, not fraud).

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-ACH-SELFAPPROVE, INV-02-ACH-PATTERN to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: A documented emergency-process exception, low value.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the exception; document; recommend control fix.
Escalate to fraud/compliance; hold/reverse the payments; review the user's transactions; open IR.
Fix the maker-checker enforcement; document the control weakness.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Identify the transactions and value; escalate to fraud/compliance if fraud-shaped.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Escalate to fraud/compliance; hold/reverse payments; review the user; open IR.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Enforce maker-checker separation in the app; alert on self-approvals; periodic SoD review.

QualityChecks.Check: USERNAME_MAKER/CHECKER are the SoD fields; type ACHAPP. Correlate value/beneficiary in the app.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Documented exception confirmed; control fix recommended.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Payments held/reversed; fraud/compliance engaged; control fixed.
